He played [[college basketball]] for the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU Mustangs]] and the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. ==High school career== Jones first attended [[Mansfield Timberview High School]]. In his junior season, he averaged 18.8 points and 9.8 rebounds and was selected first team all-district and first team all-region. In his senior season he transferred to [[Justin F. Kimball High School]] where he averaged 18.0 points and 9.0 rebounds and was named to the 2011 all-state tournament team.{{cite web|url=http://12thman.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2894|title=Texas A&M bio|work=12thMan.com|access-date=October 22, 2016}} ==College career== After graduating from high school, Jones began his collegiate career at [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|Southern Methodist University]], where he averaged 14 points and 7 rebounds per game as a sophomore. He redshirted a year and transferred to [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]].{{cite magazine|title=Jalen Jones reportedly eligible for entire Texas A&M season|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2014/10/07/jalen-jones-texas-eligible-college-basketball|access-date=September 20, 2016|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 8, 2014}} As a junior, he was named to the second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] and teamed with [[Danuel House Jr.]] to lead the Aggies to the NIT. Jones was named to the coaches' first-team All-SEC as a senior, and the Aggies reached the NCAA Tournament.{{cite news|last1=Zwerneman|first1=Brent|title=Aggies' 'alpha dogs' rarely in sync|url=http://www.expressnews.com/sports/college_sports/aggies/article/Aggies-alpha-dogs-rarely-in-sync-6880968.php|access-date=September 20, 2016|work=[[San Antonio Express-News]]|date=March 9, 2016}} He averaged 15 points and seven rebounds per game during his final season at Texas A&M.{{cite news|last1=Robb|first1=Brian|title=Celtics Round Out Training Camp Roster With Jalen Jones, Damion Lee|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2016/09/16/celtics-round-out-training-camp-roster-with-jalen-jones-damion-lee/|access-date=September 20, 2016|work=[[CBS]]|date=September 14, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Maine Red Claws (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Jones joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. In five games for the Raptors, he averaged 3.2 points and 2.0 rebounds in 8.9 minutes per game. On September 26, 2016, he signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-finalize-training-camp-roster-1|title=Celtics Finalize Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}} However, he was waived by the Celtics on October 20 after appearing in two preseason games.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/celtics/status/789206808367726594|title=The Celtics have waived Marcus Georges-Hunt...|work=Twitter|date=October 20, 2016|access-date=October 20, 2016}} On October 31, Jones was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Celtics.{{cite web|url=http://maine.dleague.nba.com/news/2016-training-camp-roster/|title=2016 Training Camp Roster Announced|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 2, 2016|archive-date=November 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104004654/http://maine.dleague.nba.com/news/2016-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2017–2018)=== Jones was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on August 2, 2017.{{cite news|title=Pelicans sign Jalen Jones to two-way contract |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-jalen-jones-two-way-contract|work=[[New Orleans Pelicans]]|date=August 2, 2017|access-date=August 2, 2017}} For the majority of this season, Jones would split his playing time between New Orleans and a [[NBA G League|G-League]] affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]]. On January 8, 2018, Jones was waived by the Pelicans.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-two-way-forward-jalen-jones|title=Pelicans waive two-way forward Jalen Jones|work=NBA.com|date=January 8, 2018|access-date=January 8, 2018}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2018)=== He signed a two-way contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on January 11, 2018.{{cite web|title=Learning with the Legends: Jalen Jones, Kyle Collinsworth, and Johnathan Motley|url=https://www.mavs.com/learning-legends-jalen-jones-kyle-collinsworth-johnathan-motley/|website=mavs.com|access-date=January 11, 2018|date=January 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113035454/https://www.mavs.com/learning-legends-jalen-jones-kyle-collinsworth-johnathan-motley/|archive-date=January 13, 2018|url-status=dead}} Throughout the rest of the year, he split his playing time between the Mavericks and their G League affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]]. He was waived by the Mavericks on July 14, 2018.{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign Kostas Antetokounmpo to two-way contract; waive Jalen Jones|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-kostas-antetokounmpo-to-two-way-contract-waive-jalen-jones/|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2018}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers/Canton Charge (2018–2019)=== On December 2, 2018, Jones was signed to a two-way contract by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. Under the terms of the deal, he splits time between the Cavs and their G League affiliate, the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/jones-blossomgame-signing-181202|title=Cavs Sign Jalen Jones and Jaron Blossomgame to Two-Way Contracts|work=NBA.com|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=December 2, 2018}} On January 15, 2019, Jones was waived by the Cavaliers.{{cite web|title=Cavs Sign Deng Adel to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/adel-signing-190115|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 16, 2019|date=January 15, 2019}} === Baskonia (2019)=== On January 22, 2019, Jones signed with [[Saski Baskonia|Kirolbet Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]] until the end of the season.{{cite news |title=Baskonia signs Jalen Jones |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/baskonia-signs-jalen-jones/ |access-date=January 22, 2019 |work=Sportando |date=January 22, 2019 |archive-date=January 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123071444/https://sportando.basketball/en/baskonia-signs-jalen-jones/ |url-status=dead }} ===Capital City Go-Go (2019–2020)=== On October 16, 2019, the [[Washington Wizards]] announced that they had signed Jones.{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Jones and Pasecniks|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-jalen-jones-anzejs-pasecniks|date=October 16, 2019|website=nba.com|access-date=October 16, 2019}} He was waived three days later. He was then added to the roster of the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |last1=Rakusin |first1=Kelly |title=GO-GO ANNOUNCE DRAFT PICKS, TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-draft-picks-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 4, 2019 |date=October 27, 2019 |archive-date=December 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209190149/https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-draft-picks-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }} Jones tallied 30 points, seven rebounds and two assists on November 10 in a win over the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].{{cite news |title=Jalen Jones: Fabulous outing in win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jalen-jones-fabulous-outing-in-win/ |access-date=January 22, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=November 10, 2019}} He missed a game against the [[College Park Skyhawks]] on December 12 with a leg injury.{{cite news |title=Jalen Jones: DNP with leg injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jalen-jones-dnp-with-leg-injury/ |access-date=January 22, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 13, 2019}} On January 26, 2020, Jones scored 22 points and added seven rebounds, three assists and one block in a loss to the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite news |title=Jalen Jones: Leads team in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jalen-jones-leads-team-in-loss/ |access-date=February 9, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 26, 2020}} He averaged 19 points and 8 rebounds per game. ===Pallacanestro Varese (2020–2022)=== On November 9, 2020, Jones signed with [[Pallacanestro Varese]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{cite web |title=Openjobmetis Varese announces Jalen Jones |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/openjobmetis-varese-announces-jalen-jones/ |website=Sportando |access-date=November 9, 2020 |date=November 9, 2020 |last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }} On November 16, it was announced that he would undergo season-ending surgery following the rupture of the Achilles tendon in his left leg.{{cite web |title=Varese: Jalen Jones(torn Achilles) will undergo season ending surgery. |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/varese-jalen-jonestorn-achilles-will-undergo-season-ending-surgery/ |website=Sportando |access-date=November 16, 2020 |date=November 16, 2020 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} The [[Lega Basket Serie A|Lega Basket]] communicated on January 8, that Jones was excluded from the rest of the [[2020–21 LBA season|2020–21 season]].{{cite web |title=Nuovi Tesseramenti e Risoluzioni |url=http://web.legabasket.it/news/127001/nuovi_tesseramenti_e_risoluzioni |publisher=legabasket.it |date=January 8, 2021 |language=Italian |access-date=January 8, 2021
